text:
Have you ever started a job without a clear position or title at all? 

My interview at Speed and Function had no job description and no technical assessment.

Just a coffee with the CEO and a department head. We talked about spiral dynamics, organizational development, and how we see the world. We also discussed my idea of creating a new department within the company.

That was it. I got the offer.

The plan was clear: join pre-sales, win deals, and fill my new department with projects. But the idea was shattered by reality.

I discovered that the company had solid revenue, loyal clients, and strong referrals – but zero marketing function. No strategy. No content pipeline. A website that was essentially a single page with almost no information. Not even anyone responsible for sales. Every client in the company’s history had come through referrals and the CEO’s personal network.

My department plan had no foundation to stand on.
When I raised this with leadership, the response was 5 words:

“Define your own role”.

Within two months, I became the marketing manager. Nobody assigned me. The role emerged from the intersection of what the company needed and what I could bring.

Speed and Function does hire for specific roles, especially developers. But in my case, the company hired for values and trusted me to find where I could contribute most. The result was a capability nobody had planned for.

That's what happens in a teal organization with a real culture of trust and self-organization. You don't fill positions. You create the conditions for the right things to emerge.

Not every organization works this way. But some do. And it changes things.
